title: Estimating the Causal Impact of Social Navigation Signals in Corridor Scenarios
abstract: arXiv:2610.16411v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Deploying robots in human-shared environments requires deciding not only how to navigate, but also when dedicated social signals are worth emitting. Classic observation-based inference can be misleading in such settings: confounding factors may bias the estimated relationship between a signal and the task outcome, leading to incorrect decisions. Causal inference provides a framework for disentangling these relationships by modelling the mechanisms linking observations, actions, and outcomes, and by estimating interventional effects after accounting for confounding paths. We study a human-robot interaction scenario in a corridor and use a causal model to estimate whether a social navigation signal causally improves transit success. We represent the interaction as a causal DAG involving robot action, pedestrian occupancy, available space, task outcome, and a controlled confounder (static obstacles). translated_title: 估计走廊场景中社交导航信号的因果影响
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.16411v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：在人类共享环境中部署机器人，不仅需要决定如何导航，还需要决定何时值得发出专门的社交信号。经典的基于观察的推断方法在此类场景中可能产生误导：混杂因素可能会使估计的信号与任务结果之间的关系产生偏差，从而导致错误的决策。因果推断提供了一个框架，通过建模连接观察、动作和结果的机制，并在考虑混杂路径后估计干预效应，从而理清这些关系。我们研究了走廊中的人机交互场景，并使用因果模型来估计社交导航信号是否在因果意义上提高了通行成功率。我们将该交互过程表示为一个因果有向无环图（DAG），其中涉及机器人动作、行人占用、可用空间、任务结果以及一个受控混杂因素（静态障碍物）。我们对干预估计进行了比较。
tldr: 本文通过构建因果有向无环图（DAG）并采用因果推断方法，在控制混杂因素（如静态障碍物）的情况下，估计走廊场景中社交导航信号是否真正因果性地提高了机器人的通行成功率。
en_tdlr: This paper constructs a causal DAG and applies causal inference to estimate whether social navigation signals causally improve robot transit success in corridor scenarios, accounting for confounding factors such as static obstacles.
